THE HEADLINES::

  1. India and Nepal announce major connectivity, energy and development projects during Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s visit.

  2. World Health Organisation congratulates India on administering over ten million doses of HPV vaccine to 14-year-old girls.

  3. European Commission proposes new sanctions on Russia targeting banks, crypto and sports events.

India and Nepal have announced a series of initiatives covering connectivity, energy, trade, education, healthcare and institutional cooperation during Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s State visit to India. The outcomes include a development cooperation package worth 15,000 crore rupees, new cross-border infrastructure projects, expanded access to Indian ports for Nepal’s transit cargo and eight Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) across key sectors.

         

 

 

 

 

 

Among the major announcements is the launch of the Sarayu-Kamala Express rail service connecting Ayodhya in India with Janakpur in Nepal.

         

 

 

 

 

India and Nepal have adopted a joint vision laying roadmap for a future-oriented partnership between the two countries. New Delhi also announced development package worth 24,000 crore Nepali rupees for the Himalayan nation. Both the countries signed eight agreements for collaboration in different fields including Health, traditional medicine, establishment of satellite communication network and capacity building training programme among others. The agreements were signed after talks between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah in New Delhi yesterday. Both leaders held wide ranging discussions on bilateral, regional and global issues.

         

 

 

 

 

Later in joint press statement, Prime Minister Modi said, India-Nepal relations are woven together by shared history, faith, culture and deep people-to-people ties. He also announced the Joint vision adopted by the two nations.

         

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Our correspondent has filed this report:

         

“Prime Minister Narendra Modi reaffirmed India’s unwavering support to Nepal’s development journey as a close friend and neighbour. The Joint Press Release on the State Visit of the Prime Minister of Nepal said that India will extend development assistance of 15,000 crore rupees comprising a grant assistance of 3,500 crore rupees for post-disaster reconstruction and new infrastructure projects in Nepal. It will also extend a Rupee-denominated Line of Credit of 11,500 crore rupees for energy sector projects. Specific projects as well as modalities for the provision of development assistance will be finalized through mutual consultations. Both leaders expressed satisfaction at the ongoing progress in the implementation of development projects in Nepal, including the High Impact Community Development Projects. Suparna Saikia, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

World Health Organisation (WHO) has congratulated India on administering over ten million doses of the HPV vaccine to 14-year-old girls. In a social media post, WHO described it as a significant milestone in the country’s efforts to prevent cervical cancer. It said that this achievement reflects the collective commitment of the Government, health workers, communities, parents and partners to protect girls from cervical cancer and ensure that every girl has access to the protection offered by HPV vaccination.

 

 

 

Earlier, Prime Minister Narendra Modi also commended all the stakeholders for their efforts in ensuring the administration of one crore HPV vaccine doses, covering nearly 87 percent of annual cohort of eligible girls. Sharing a social media post of Union Health Minister JP Nadda, Mr Modi said it is a significant milestone in the journey towards preventive healthcare.

Union Agriculture and Rural Development Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said India’s extreme poverty rate has fallen from 27.1 per cent to 2.6 per cent, with nearly 500 million people moving out of poverty.

         

 

 

 

 

Citing a recent World Bank report, Mr Chouhan said the government’s next task was to ensure that those who had moved above the poverty line did not fall back, while improving the lives of those still left behind.

S&P Global has projected India to be the fastest-growing economy in the Asia-Pacific region in 2027. The agency expects India’s economy to grow by 7 per cent in both the current fiscal year and the next fiscal year, ending March 2028. In its Economic Outlook Asia-Pacific Q1 2027 report, agency said India’s growth in the June and September quarters was driven by robust goods exports, government-led investment spending and strong household consumption, supported by buoyant credit growth.

Indian Railways has operated around eighteen thousand additional trains during the festive seasons from October to November this year accommodating lakhs of passengers daily. The Indian Railways said that during the peak festive period of 26 days, around 20 crore passengers travelled in trains, registering an increase of 8 per cent over the corresponding period last year.

 

 

 

 

 

         

 

 

 

 

Guru Nanak Jayanti, also known as Gurpurab, is being celebrated with great religious fervour and devotion across the country and around the world today. The festival marks the 557th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the first Sikh Guru and founder of Sikhism. Guru Nanak Jayanti is observed on the full moon day of the Kartik month, as per the lunar calendar. More from our correspondent:

         

 

 

 

“Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji gave the message of – Ek Onkar – One God – and opposed the social evils like casteism and emphasized that all human beings are equal. On this auspicious occasion, a large number of devotees are paying obeisance at Gurdwaras across the country since morning. Gurdwara Ber Sahib at Sultanpur Lodhi, in Punjab, where Guru Sahib meditated for 14 years, 9 months and 13 days, is reverberating with hymns as Kirtan Darbars and Gurbani Vichar are going on here and at other Gurudwaras including at Sri Harmandir Sahib in Amritsar. An inner joy of connecting with the God is visible on the faces of the devotees. Community Kitchens are also going on at various places. Rajesh Bali, Akashvani News, Jalandhar.”

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the Sikh tradition has always symbolised the spirit of sacrificing everything for the nation and its culture. The Prime Minister said this while attending Shabad Kirtan at Lok Niwas, the residence of Lieutenant Governor of Delhi Taranjit Singh Sandhu in New Delhi. Quoting Guru Nanak Dev’s teachings, the Prime Minister said Guru Nanak Dev’s principles have been an integral part of his life. Mr Modi said that during the most difficult periods of India’s history, the Sikh Gurus kept alive the flame of national protection and cultural identity.

         

 

 

 

 

The Prime Minister said this year’s Prakash Parv holds special significance as it marks 350 years of the martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur. He said Guru Tegh Bahadur sacrificed his life on the soil of Delhi to protect the identity of the nation, faith, beliefs and values.

President Droupadi Murmu has extended greetings to all Indians living in India and abroad on the occasion of Prakash Parv. In a social media post, the President said that the message of Ik Onkar given by Guru Nanak Dev is a message of unity for all humanity.

In Uttar Pradesh, Ghats of holy rivers are brimming with pilgrims reaching for the auspicious bathing on the occasion of Kartik Poornima today. Preparations are also in full swing for the celebration of Dev Deepawali at Varanasi. A report:

 

        

“Devotes have thronged to the ghats to take holy dip in rivers like Ganga, Yamuna and Saryu. In the temple city Ayodhya more than 10 lakh pilgrims are expected to reach and administration has made elaborate arrangements for them. Oher major cities like Varanasi, prayagraj, Kanpur, Kannauj and Hapur are also witnessing heavy rush of pilgrims since early morning.  Ghats of Ganga in Varanasi and Mandakini in Chitrakoot district are being prepared for the spectacular Dev Deepawali Mahotsav. 84 Ghats of holy river Ganga in Varanasi will be illuminated with the light of more than 10 lakh earthen lamps this evening.

         

 

 

 

 

This year, along with the traditional Deepotsav, 2,100 indigenous drones, a laser show and eco-friendly fireworks will also make the celebration special. SUSHIL CHANDRA TIWARI, AKASHVANI NEWS, LUCKNOW.”

President Droupadi Murmu is arriving in Odisha today on a two-day visit during which she will attend two important programmes in the state. The President will be the chief guest at the historic Bali Yatra festival in Cuttack this evening. During her visit to Cuttack, President Murmu is scheduled to travel by boat from the Silver City Boat Club along the Mahanadi river to the Bali Yatra venue. She will then proceed to the festival grounds and inaugurate the annual fair, which celebrates Odisha’s glorious maritime history and the centuries-old trading links of Odia seafarers with Southeast Asian countries, including Bali.

20th edition of WAVES Film Bazaar will concludes today at the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. The five-day marketplace organized by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC)  celebrated two decades of connecting Indian and South Asian cinema with international producers, buyers, and distributors. This year’s programme featured the Co-Production Market, NFDC Screenwriters’ Lab, Work-in-Progress Lab, Viewing Room, Market Screenings, and Producers’ Lab. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

 

 

Initiated in 2007 with just 204 delegates as Film Bazaar, Now in the form of WAVES Film Bazar it has grown bigger and better. It is now one of South Asia’s leading platforms for film business and international collaboration. WAVES Bazaar connects creative talent with stakeholders across India’s media and entertainment ecosystem.

         

 

 

 

 

“An important outcome at the 20th edition of WAVES Film Bazar was the signing of an MoU between The National Film Development Corporation and Sony Pictures Networks India. It launched the WAVES Bazaar × SPNI Content Creator Submission Initiative, opening opportunities for writers, creators and production houses to pitch original fiction and non-fiction concepts in five languages.

         

 

 

 

 

Artists, creators submitted content in formats like fiction series, premium TV+ content, reality shows, game and competition formats, talent-based programmes and other unscripted concepts.

         

 

 

 

 

Another major highlight today at IFFI 2026 is the awards ceremony of the first edition of ‘Page se Pitch Tak’. With Alex and Vishnu, This is Saira Mujtaba, IFFI GOA.”

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will hold bilateral talks with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah at Hyderabad House in New Delhi today. Both leaders will review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest. The two Prime Ministers will virtually inaugurate several completed initiatives apart from carrying out foundation stone laying ceremonies for some new projects. A number of forward-looking bilateral documents in diverse areas are expected to be concluded and exchanged following the talks. The major outcomes are likely to be in the domains of development partnership, energy, hydropower, railways, connectivity, addressing climate change and disaster resilience, infrastructure, and technology.

         

 

The visiting dignitary arrived in the natoional capital yesterday on a two day visit. He will be accorded a ceremonial welcome at Rashtrapati Bhavan this morning. The Nepal Prime Minister will pay his respects to Mahatma Gandhi by laying wreath at Rajghat. He will call on President Droupadi Murmu later this afternoon. Our correspondent reports that this is Prime Minister Balendra Shah’s first bilateral visit.

 

         

 

“This visit has come at an opportune moment when there is considerable synergy between the national priorities of both countries in terms of economic growth, social development, expansion of infrastructure, adoption of technology, and addressing issues such as natural disasters and climate change. The discussions between the two leaders will provide a political direction which is expected to chart the course for the bilateral partnership for the coming years. India and Nepal enjoy unique and comprehensive relations characterized by mutual trust, open borders, shared traditions and close people-to-people ties. India is Nepal’s largest trade, transit and investment partner and the neighbouring nation enjoys duty-free access to the Indian market. India is the largest source of foreign tourists to Nepal and both sides are working to promote shared circuits such as the Ramayana Circuit and the Buddhist Circuit. Suparna Saikia, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and  Prime Minister  of Nepal Balendra Shah will jointly  flag off the new weekly train service between Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh and Janakpur Dham in Nepal  through video conferencing from New Delhi today. The  train service named Saryu- Kamla Express, introduced by the Indian Railways, will establish an important rail link between two destinations deeply associated with the Ramayana tradition – Janakpur Dham, revered as the birthplace of Mata Sita, and Ayodhya, the birthplace of Lord Shri Ram. The initiative will provide passengers from both countries with improved access to these prominent religious and cultural centres while reinforcing their shared civilizational heritage. Our correspondent reports that it is a major step of Indian Railways towards strengthening cross-border connectivity, religious tourism  and India-Nepal Friendship.

 

         

 

“The  Saryu- Kamla Express  will operate once a week, with its originating days being  Monday from Ayodhya Cantt. and Saturday from Janakpur Dham. Covering nearly  604 kilometres, the weekly service will connect Janakpur Dham with Ayodhya Cantt while passing through several important towns and cities in Uttar Pradesh  and Bihar. The new service is expected to make cross-border travel more convenient for pilgrims, tourists and other passengers. It will facilitate religious journeys between Janakpur and Ayodhya, encourage tourism circuits associated with the Ramayana and provide greater mobility to people travelling for education, business and family-related purposes.India and Nepal share centuries-old cultural, historical and social bonds, with religious traditions and cross-border community relationships forming an integral part of this partnership. The new train service will add another dimension to bilateral cooperation by using railway connectivity to bring communities closer. Anand Kumar for Akashvani News,“ Ayodhya.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah has said that the development of the Northeast and employment generation for young people remains a top priority for the Narendra Modi government. Launching four major development initiatives worth more than 5,610 crore rupees in Arunachal Pradesh, Mr Shah said the Centre is working to strengthen infrastructure and improve access to essential services in the region, especially in villages along the international border.

         

 

Highlighting the Vibrant Villages Programme, he said the government has changed the perception of border settlements from the country’s “last villages” to its “first villages”, underscoring their strategic and developmental importance. Mr Shah noted that the programme was initially taken up in villages in Arunachal Pradesh along the China border. He said, Mobile Medical Units have also been deployed across 11 border districts, equipped with telemedicine facilities, AI-based portable tuberculosis screening, digital X-ray machines, ECG equipment and modern laboratories. Home Minister said the Northeast has witnessed significant improvements in connectivity over the past 12 years, with the region’s state capitals now connected through rail and air services.

Ten films will compete for the prestigious ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal at the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa this year. The award recognizes films that reflect Mahatma Gandhi’s ideals of non-violence, tolerance, intercultural understanding and a culture of peace. The ten films selected for this year’s competition bring together stories from diverse cultural backgrounds, highlighting human relationships, social challenges and shared values. More from our correspondent:

 

         

 

The ten films selected for this year’s competition explore a wide range of contemporary social realities, including gender inequality, human relationships, social justice, compassion, friendship and the challenges of a rapidly changing world.  India is represented by three films – Sarfaraz Alam’s Kabir Sir ka Akhri Lesson, Kannan S.’s Scroll and Muskan Asthana’s Sev Micchar. Among today’s highlights, Turkish filmmakers Faysal Soysal’s Rahma and Elif Ada’s The Farm will be screened. Among other films that will be screened during the nineday festival are Emily Atef’s Call Me Queen, Gessica Généus’s Marie Madeleine, Amartei Armar’s Our Time Will Come, Laïla Marrakchi’s Strawberries, and Lu Po-Shun’s Will You Still Be My Friend. The four-member international jury, headed by Algerian filmmaker and film critic Professor Ahmed Bedjaoui, will Judge the entries. Through this showcase, IFFI reinforces cinema’s ability to go beyond entertainment and become a powerful medium for dialogue, empathy and social change – values that lie at the heart of the ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal. With Alex Dhissa and Vishnu, this is Saira Mujtaba, IFFI GOA.

This year’s United Nations Climate Change Conference, COP31, at Antalya in Turkiye ended yesterday with no agreement for the first time since 2009. The UN climate talks collapsed without an overarching agreement after deep disagreements over whether to explicitly mention fossil fuels in the final text. European Union and several other countries rejected the proposed deal, saying it is too weak to advance the fight against climate change. More from our correspondent::

 

 

         

“The two-week negotiations, known as COP31, continued nearly 48 hours beyond their scheduled conclusion, making them the longest COP on record. However, countries failed to reach a consensus on a main agreement, known as a cover decision, amid irreconcilable differences over fossil fuels, climate finance and other contentious issues. Disagreements over explicitly mentioning fossil fuels and providing financial support to developing countries ultimately prevented governments from reaching an overarching agreement. European Union, along with several countries, refused to accept the final proposal put forward by the joint Turkish-Australian leadership because it did not explicitly mention fossil fuels. Fossil fuels remained one of the biggest sticking points throughout the negotiations, with Saudi Arabia and other major oil-producing countries lobbying against their inclusion in the final document.jigyasa pandey, Akashvani News, Delhi.

In Jammu and Kashmir, the 10-day Jhiri Mela, which is celebrated at Jhiri village in Marh block in the outskirts of Jammu city, will begin today. Held annually in the honor of Baba Jitto and Bua Kodi, the Mela draws pilgrims and visitors from Jammu region and neighboring states including Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and Himachal Pradesh. This Mela is associated with the supreme sacrifice of 16th century Dogra hero and revolutionary and honest farmer, Baba Jitto who was a great devotee of Mata Vaishno Devi. This event is a platform to promote local craftsmen and highlight traditional arts for visitors from beyond J&K. The event is vital not only for local agriculture but for showcasing Jammu’s cultural heritage. A report:

 

         

 

“Baba Jito fought against injustice and laid down his life after he was cheated by the landlord of the area and sacrificed his life for justice and righteousness. The Mela is anticipated to attract about 15 lakh visitors, making it an opportunity for government departments to actively promote schemes and programmes that benefit rural populations. Various Government departments have set up specialised kiosks to provide information on relevant government schemes, ensuring farmers’ welfare remains central. This event is a platform to promote local craftsmen and highlight traditional arts for visitors from beyond Jammu & Kashmir and is vital not only for local agriculture but for showcasing Jammu’s cultural heritage. N. Gulshan Raina For Akashvani News from Jammu.”

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed happiness over people buying less gold following an appeal made by him last year. Addressing a function in Lucknow, Mr Modi said, people cut back on buying gold after his appeal, which helped bring gold prices down and allowed buyers to save money.

 

The Prime Minister had appealed to the nation to avoid buying gold, when India’s foreign exchange came under pressure with the West Asia conflict pushing up crude prices. Mr Modi drew a parallel between the public’s response to his appeal and how Indians historically heeded former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri’s call to skip one meal, stating that the country still holds that same character.

 

Gold prices have seen a major decline over the past few months. 24-carat gold prices fell to 12,523 rupees per gram yesterday from 15,250 per gram on May 9, this year. Gold imports fell nearly forty percent during April-October 2026.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah has stressed the need for better coordination between Central and State security agencies to maintain peace and security in Arunachal Pradesh. He called for strengthening the local intelligence network and ensuring continuous monitoring of sensitive areas.

 

Considering the strategic importance of Arunachal Pradesh’s nearly 1,126-kilometre-long international border with China, Mr. Shah also reviewed border security arrangements and the development of strategic infrastructure along the frontier.

 

Mr. Shah chaired a high-level review meeting at Lok Bhavan in Itanagar yesterday to discuss key issues relating to law and order, internal security, border management and development in the Northeastern state.

He said this while addressing the Fourth Annual General Meeting of the BRIC Society in New Delhi yesterday. Dr Singh said that India’s biotechnology transformation has contributed significantly to the country’s development journey, reflecting the expanding role of science, innovation and technology in national growth.

Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Gajendra Singh Shekhawat has said that historical connections have played a significant role in bringing Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) countries closer to one another. Addressing the joint sessions on the second day of the first SCO Civilizational Dialogue Forum in New Delhi yesterday, he said civilisations are not merely legacies of the past but living traditions whose knowledge continues to illuminate the present and inspire future generations.

 

Mr Shekhawat emphasised that the shared civilizational knowledge and heritage should be harnessed to advance collective efforts through dialogue, institutional partnerships, cultural exchanges, and meaningful cooperation.

Tomorrow, the visiting leader will call on President Droupadi Murmu and also meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi. During the bilateral talks, both Prime Ministers will review the full range of India-Nepal relations and exchange views on regional and international issues of mutual interest. Our correspondent reports that Memorandum of Understanding in various areas will also be exchanged between the two countries.

 

”The Ministry of External Affairs has said that the visit continues the tradition of regular high-level exchanges between the two countries and reflects the importance India attaches to its relations with Nepal under its ‘Neighbourhood First’ policy. It added that the visit will provide an opportunity to further strengthen the bilateral partnership and advance mutually beneficial cooperation.

 

The Ministry further said that India and Nepal share close and friendly relations, rooted in historical, cultural and civilisational links and strong people-to-people ties. Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors including trade and commerce, energy and water resources, and digital connectivity.
